regions.label: Germany
regions.note: Standalone by business grouping - deliberately not merged into DACH.

regions.label: France
regions.note: Standalone by business grouping - not part of Benelux, Southern Europe or DACH.

regions.label: DACH
regions.note: Switzerland and Austria only - Germany is its own region by business grouping.

regions.label: Eastern Europe
regions.note: Working list - extend here when a live signal names an Eastern European country not listed.

regions.label: North America
regions.note: Simplified to continent - any other North American ISO code falls back here.

regions.label: South America
regions.note: Simplified to continent - resolved by the ISO continent fallback.

regions.label: Africa
regions.note: Simplified to continent - resolved by the ISO continent fallback.

regions.label: Asia
regions.note: Simplified to continent - resolved by the ISO continent fallback.

regions.label: Oceania
regions.note: Simplified to continent - resolved by the ISO continent fallback.

regions.label: Global / Cross-region
regions.note: EU-wide regulation, worldwide statements, or signals spanning several regions with no dominant one. Set explicitly, never inferred from an absent country.

use_cases.label: Predictive maintenance
use_cases.definition: Anticipating equipment failures from operational or sensor data to schedule maintenance before breakdown.

use_cases.label: Asset tracking
use_cases.definition: Locating and monitoring the status of physical assets across sites or supply chains.

use_cases.label: Production scheduling
use_cases.definition: Optimizing the sequencing and allocation of manufacturing or production runs.

use_cases.label: Automated inspection / defect detection
use_cases.definition: Automated visual or physical inspection of products, equipment, or infrastructure to detect defects or damage, including imaging analytics.

use_cases.label: Anomaly detection
use_cases.definition: Detecting abnormal patterns in system, network, or transactional data streams, including cybersecurity threats. Excludes visual/physical inspection (see automated-inspection-defect-detection).

use_cases.label: Warehouse automation
use_cases.definition: Automating storage, picking, and material handling operations in warehouses.

use_cases.label: Business forecasting
use_cases.definition: Predicting future demand, sales, or revenue to support planning decisions.

use_cases.label: Dynamic pricing
use_cases.definition: Adjusting prices automatically based on demand, competition, or market conditions.

use_cases.label: Inventory optimization
use_cases.definition: Determining optimal stock levels and replenishment to reduce cost and stockouts.

use_cases.label: Route optimization
use_cases.definition: Computing optimal routes or tours for delivery, transport, or field operations.

use_cases.label: Workforce scheduling
use_cases.definition: Optimizing staff shift planning and resource allocation against demand.

use_cases.label: Customer service automation
use_cases.definition: Automating customer support interactions (chatbots, voice assistants, ticket handling).

use_cases.label: Personalized recommendations
use_cases.definition: Suggesting products, content, or actions tailored to individual users.

use_cases.label: Customer segmentation
use_cases.definition: Grouping customers by behavior or value for targeting and strategy.

use_cases.label: Churn prediction
use_cases.definition: Identifying customers at risk of leaving to enable retention actions.

use_cases.label: Sentiment analysis
use_cases.definition: Extracting opinions and emotional tone from text, reviews, or social media.

use_cases.label: Fraud detection
use_cases.definition: Identifying fraudulent transactions, claims, or behavior in real time or batch.

use_cases.label: Risk scoring
use_cases.definition: Quantifying the risk of counterparties, credit, or operations to support decisions, including credit underwriting.

use_cases.label: KYC/AML automation
use_cases.definition: Automating identity verification and anti-money-laundering checks.

use_cases.label: Compliance monitoring
use_cases.definition: Continuously verifying operations against regulatory or internal rules.

use_cases.label: Document processing / extraction
use_cases.definition: Extracting and structuring information from documents (contracts, invoices, claims, forms).

use_cases.label: IT operations automation
use_cases.definition: Automating IT infrastructure monitoring, incident response, and routine operations (AIOps).

use_cases.label: Diagnostic support
use_cases.definition: Assisting clinical diagnosis or patient prioritization/triage with data-driven insight.

use_cases.label: Precision agriculture
use_cases.definition: Optimizing farming inputs and yields using field-level data.

use_cases.label: Network optimization
use_cases.definition: Optimizing capacity, coverage, and performance of telecom or utility networks.

use_cases.label: Energy optimization
use_cases.definition: Reducing or shifting the energy consumption of buildings, industry, or grids.

use_cases.label: Environmental/emissions monitoring
use_cases.definition: Measuring and reporting environmental impact, emissions, or pollution.

technologies.label: Cloud Data Platform
technologies.definition: Cloud-based infrastructure for storing, integrating, and analyzing data at scale, including data lakes and warehouses.

technologies.label: Edge Computing
technologies.definition: Processing data locally near its source instead of in a central cloud.

technologies.label: Digital Twin
technologies.definition: Virtual real-time replica of a physical asset, process, or system used for simulation and monitoring.

technologies.label: IoT Platforms
technologies.definition: Platforms connecting and managing networks of sensors and devices, including sensor networks and telematics.

technologies.label: RFID / Asset Tagging
technologies.definition: Tag-based identification and tracking of physical items (passive or active tags).

technologies.label: 5G Connectivity
technologies.definition: High-bandwidth, low-latency mobile connectivity enabling real-time industrial use cases.

technologies.label: Machine Learning
technologies.definition: Statistical or deep learning models trained on data for prediction or classification. Excludes content generation (see generative-ai-llms) and image understanding (see computer-vision).

technologies.label: Computer Vision
technologies.definition: Interpreting images or video: recognition, detection, measurement.

technologies.label: Natural Language Processing
technologies.definition: Analyzing and understanding text or language: classification, extraction, translation. Excludes content generation (see generative-ai-llms).

technologies.label: Generative AI / LLMs
technologies.definition: Large language and generative models producing text, code, or images, or acting as reasoning agents.

technologies.label: Speech Recognition
technologies.definition: Converting spoken audio into text or voice commands.

technologies.label: Reinforcement Learning
technologies.definition: Agents learning optimal decisions through trial-and-error interaction with an environment.

technologies.label: Robotic Process Automation
technologies.definition: Software bots automating repetitive, rule-based digital tasks. No physical robots (see industrial-robotics).

technologies.label: Industrial Robotics
technologies.definition: Physical robots performing manufacturing or industrial tasks.

technologies.label: Warehouse Automation Systems
technologies.definition: Physical automation hardware for warehouses: AS/RS, AGVs, sorters.

technologies.label: Autonomous Vehicles / Drones
technologies.definition: Self-navigating vehicles or drones for transport, inspection, or delivery.

technologies.label: Blockchain / Distributed Ledger
technologies.definition: Shared tamper-evident ledgers for traceability or decentralized transactions.

technologies.label: Cybersecurity Platform
technologies.definition: Security tooling protecting systems and data, including zero trust architectures and biometric authentication.

technologies.label: Digital Payments Infrastructure
technologies.definition: Systems enabling electronic payment processing and settlement.

technologies.label: E-invoicing / Peppol Integration
technologies.definition: Structured electronic invoicing exchanged via standards such as Peppol.

technologies.label: AR/VR Platforms
technologies.definition: Augmented or virtual reality for training, visualization, or remote assistance.
